docs.title: DecisionTrace
docs.text:
Record why your AI made a decision, at the moment it's made — then ask dt why later.

Logs tell you what an agent did. DecisionTrace records why it was allowed to: the request and inputs, the rules that passed or failed, exceptions and who granted them, the options it rejected, who approved, and what happened next. Local, append-only, tamper-evident.

pipx install liquicent-decisiontrace
dt install claude-code
# …work as usual…
dt log
dt why <id | file | commit>
  • New here? Getting started
  • What exactly is recorded? Concepts
  • Using an SDK, MCP or OpenTelemetry? Adapters
  • Worried about what's stored? Privacy & security

docs.title: CLI reference
docs.text: Run dt <command> --help for every option. Global option: --home PATH (or DT_HOME) selects the store directory (default ~/.decisiontrace).

docs.title: Recording
docs.text: Command What it does dt init Create the local store (safe to run again). dt install Start recording: claude-code (hooks), or claude-desktop / cursor (MCP server). --scope user\|project\|local for Claude Code. dt uninstall Stop recording (recorded decisions are kept). dt mcp Run the local MCP server (stdio), print client setup with --config claude-desktop\|cursor\|claude-code, or serve a team over HTTP with --http (self-hosted MCP); --new-token prints a token. dt ingest-otel Receive OpenTelemetry GenAI spans (OTLP/HTTP on port 4318), or --file OTLP JSON. dt append Validate, redact and append records from .json / .jsonl files (all or nothing). dt drain Move queued Claude Code hook events into the store now (normally automatic).

docs.title: Recall
docs.text: Command What it does dt log List recent decisions, newest first (-n, --kind, --since). dt show One decision with rules, exceptions, alternatives, approvals and outcome (--json). dt why Plain-English account of a decision, by id, file path or git commit. dt similar Rank past decisions by similarity, with the P, X, C, A, T, Δt breakdown. dt ask Ask a question about your decisions. Works offline; --llm uses Claude. dt outcomes (dt outcomes detect) Fill in outcomes from the store, git (--git) and business events (--events --preset stripe\|zendesk\|jira\|github\|pagerduty); see outcome detection. --vwu records accepted delivery signals as verified work units (--vwu-window-days). dt outcome Record what happened after a decision (--accepted, --reverted, --overridden, --escalated, --failed, --complained, --note, --value-usd). With --accepted --vwu UNIT, also a verified work unit (--verified-by, --reversal-days, --reversal-cost, --quantity, --quality-metric, --quality-threshold, --quality-value, --quality-direction). dt vwu List verified work units with their state: provisional, final or reverted (--since, --state, --json); the footer gives the share verified without a person.

docs.title: Integrity and data
docs.text: Command What it does dt verify Recompute the hash chain and report any tampering. dt export Export every record, oldest first, with its hash-chain fields (--jsonl, -o). dt validate Check records against the schema and the Python models (without storing them). dt reindex Rebuild search indexes and compute missing embeddings (if enabled). dt eval Score dt why against a hand-checked golden set, or draft one with --sample N. dt schema Print the path of the DecisionTrace JSON Schema. dt version Show the package and schema versions.

docs.title: A decision record
docs.text:
Every decision is DT = ⟨C, P, E, X, H, T, O⟩, plus what was actually done:

Field Holds C context inputs (typed references, hashes, short redacted summaries), state before P policies each rule checked: id, version, engine, pass/fail, enforced or advisory E exceptions rules waived, by whom, why X alternatives options considered and not taken, and what rejected them H human_path requested → approved / rejected / edited / escalated, with latency T actor_time actor, on whose behalf, model, client, timestamps, tokens, cost O outcome as known at record time; later outcomes are separate records actions what was done (tool calls, API calls, file and memory writes) state_after resulting state, e.g. the git commit

decision_kind (e.g. refund.approve, code.edit) and capabilities are inferred from what happened — never declared.

docs.title: Three record types
docs.text:
• decision — the record above
  • outcome — what happened later (accepted, reverted, complained, …), linked by id; an accepted one may carry a verified work unit
  • correction — a fix to a recorded field, linked by id; views apply it, the stored decision never changes

docs.title: The store
docs.text: SQLite in ~/.decisiontrace (DT_HOME to move it). Records are append-only (triggers block UPDATE/DELETE) and hash-chained: each stores sha256(previous hash ‖ canonical JSON). dt verify recomputes the chain and reports edited, removed or reordered records.

docs.title: Links
docs.text: Decisions link to each other: delegation (an agent handing work to a subagent), hand_off, precedent, reversal, supersedes. The local store keeps the edges; the team-wide graph built from them is Liquicent's, not this project's.

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text: The short version. For every step in detail, see the user guide.

docs.title: 1. Install
docs.text:
pipx install liquicent-decisiontrace     # Python 3.11+; or: uv tool install liquicent-decisiontrace
dt init                                  # creates ~/.decisiontrace (optional: install does it)

pipx (or uv tool) gives dt its own environment and puts it on your PATH. Use it where plain pip install fails with "externally-managed-environment", as it does on Debian, Ubuntu and Homebrew Python:

sudo apt install pipx      # macOS: brew install pipx
pipx ensurepath            # then open a new terminal

In a project's virtual environment, pip install liquicent-decisiontrace works as usual. Upgrade later with pipx upgrade liquicent-decisiontrace.

docs.title: 2. Record
docs.text:
Pick the tool you already use:

dt install claude-code      # Claude Code hooks (all projects)
dt install claude-desktop   # MCP server for Claude Desktop
dt install cursor           # MCP server for Cursor

In Python: client = dt.wrap(anthropic.Anthropic()) — see SDK adapter.

docs.title: 3. Recall
docs.text:
dt log                                  # recent decisions
dt why 01M53TRF3G                       # by id (any unique prefix)
dt why src/billing/due_dates.py         # the last decision that changed this file
dt why c1a90b2                          # the decision that produced this commit
dt similar 01M53TRF3G                   # precedents, with similarity breakdown
dt ask "which refunds needed an exception last week?"

docs.title: 4. Close the loop
docs.text:
dt outcome 01M53TRF3G --reverted --note "broke month-end invoices"
dt verify

Outcomes are appended, never edited in — the original decision stays exactly as recorded.

docs.title: Try it without any setup
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/Liquicent/liquicent-decisiontrace && cd liquicent-decisiontrace
uv sync
uv run python examples/refund_agent.py
uv run dt log

docs.title: What's out of scope
docs.text:
DecisionTrace records and recalls. It deliberately does not:

  • Enforce anything. No gateway, proxy or policy engine. Your code, your permission rules and your policy engine decide; DecisionTrace records what they decided. (Authority Envelope checks are recorded, not enforced.)
  • Run as a hosted service or sync between machines.
  • Score trust or route work (TrustRank, WorkRank).
  • Build a team-wide decision graph, auto-approve from precedent, or report on how a company's decisions are trending (cost, compounding, approvals per 100 decisions).

Those need many people's traces over time; they are Liquicent's products — DecisionTrace records. Valence reveals. Liquicent learns. The local store and open schema are designed so they can read what you record here, if you choose.

docs.title: Outcome detection
docs.text:
A decision without an outcome teaches nothing, and people rarely run dt outcome. dt outcomes detect fills outcomes in from signals that already exist. It is safe to run as often as you like (for example daily from cron):

dt outcomes detect                                   # signals inside the store
dt outcomes detect --git ~/src/app                   # + git reverts and merges
dt outcomes detect --events zendesk.jsonl --preset zendesk
dt outcomes detect --events stripe-events.jsonl --preset stripe --dry-run
dt outcomes detect --assume-accepted-after 14        # opt-in: silence counts as accepted
dt outcomes detect --git . --events zendesk.jsonl --preset zendesk --vwu   # + verified work units

docs.title: Sources
docs.text:
Source Signal Outcome Store a human overrode step on the decision overridden Store the decision's last action failed failed Store a later decision links to it with reversal / supersedes reverted / overridden Store a person decides the same business item (same ticket, order…) within 24 h overridden --git the decision's commit (made by it, or the first commit within 3 days touching its files) is reverted reverted --git that commit is on the main branch and survives --settle-days (3) accepted --events --preset stripe dispute → complained; refund/payment failed → failed; cancelled/voided → reverted; refunded/succeeded → accepted as listed --events --preset zendesk reopened ticket, bad satisfaction rating → complained; solved → accepted as listed --events --preset jira status → Reopened → complained; Done/Resolved/Closed → accepted; Won't Do → reverted as listed --events --preset github PR merged → accepted; closed unmerged → reverted; issue reopened → complained as listed --events --preset pagerduty incident triggered with ref or trace_id in its details → failed failed --events (generic) {"ref", "event", "at", "value_usd"?} or {"trace_id", …}; event words such as reopened, chargeback, rolled_back, failed, solved, merged mapped --assume-accepted-after N a decision that acted and has no negative signal N days later accepted (noted as an assumption)

Events match a decision when their ref equals one of its refs (context inputs, action targets, state), or when the id part after the last : # / (4+ characters) is equal — so stripe:ch_9001 matches an order recorded as shop:ch_9001, and 88412 matches zendesk:88412. Only decisions made before the event are matched.

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
• An outcome recorded by a person, or with the decision itself, is never overridden.
  • Per decision, the most serious signal wins (reverted > failed > complained > overridden > escalated > accepted). Bad news later replaces an earlier detected accepted; nothing detected ever turns a bad outcome back into a good one.
  • Detected outcomes are ordinary appended outcome records, recorded_by a system actor decisiontrace:detect:<source>, with the evidence in attributes. Their recorded_at is when the signal happened, so replays see them only from that moment.
  • Running twice records nothing new.

docs.title: Verified work units (--vwu)
docs.text:
With --vwu, an accepted outcome from a delivery signal also records a verified work unit, verified by outcome_signal:

Source Unit Reversible until --git code.change merge time + --settle-days (already passed, so the unit is final at once) --events --preset stripe stripe.payment (stripe.refund for a refund) event time + --vwu-window-days (7) --events --preset zendesk / jira / github zendesk.ticket / jira.issue / github.pull_request event time + --vwu-window-days --events (generic) the event's unit if it is a dotted label, else work.item event time + --vwu-window-days

Signals inside the store and --assume-accepted-after never make units: an assumption is not a verification. A later reverted, failed or overridden signal inside the window turns the unit to reverted (see dt vwu). Turn --vwu on from the first run: an outcome already detected without a unit is not recorded again.

docs.title: Never leaves your machine
docs.text: No account, no server, no telemetry. The only network calls are ones you ask for: dt ask --llm (sends the matching, redacted records to Anthropic) and the one-time model download if you enable embeddings.

docs.title: Redacted before anything is written
docs.text:
• Secrets removed: Anthropic, OpenAI, Stripe, GitHub, Slack, AWS and Google keys, JWTs, private keys, bearer tokens, credentials in URLs, password= / api_key: style values.
  • Personal data pseudonymised: e-mail addresses, phone numbers, cards (Luhn-checked), Indian PAN and Aadhaar (Verhoeff-checked) become [EMAIL:3f9a1c07]-style tokens keyed by a per-store salt, so traces about the same person still link.
  • The Claude Code hook redacts before writing its queue file, too.

docs.title: Not stored at all
docs.text:
• model reasoning / chain-of-thought, and assistant replies
  • prompt and response bodies (unless bodies = true in config.toml; even then redacted)
  • file contents, command output, tool results, OpenTelemetry message attributes

Records hold references, hashes and short redacted summaries instead.

docs.title: Tamper-evident, not tamper-proof
docs.text: The hash chain detects edited, deleted, inserted or reordered records. Someone who can rewrite the entire file can forge a consistent chain — so anchor it: dt verify prints the head hash; commit or publish it somewhere you trust.

docs.title: Erasure
docs.text: Optional bodies live outside the chain and can be erased without breaking dt verify. Records themselves are append-only by design; keep personal data out of them (redaction does most of this) and use namespaces to separate stores.

docs.title: Reporting a vulnerability
docs.text: See SECURITY.md.

docs.title: dt why
docs.text: A plain-English account built only from what was recorded — no model call, so it is reproducible and never invents a reason. Accepts a decision id (or prefix), a file path (the latest decision that wrote it), or a git commit (the decision whose turn produced it).

docs.title: dt similar
docs.text:
Ranks precedents with the similarity function from DecisionTrace and Context Graphs:

Sim = αP + βX + γC + δA + εT − λΔt
Term Meaning Default weight P shared rules, weighted by whether they had the same result; exceptions on the same rule α = 0.30 X the same options rejected, by the same kind of actor β = 0.10 C overlap of intent and context (plus embedding cosine if enabled) γ = 0.30 A the same actions and capabilities, same kind δ = 0.20 T same actor, actor type, model, principal ε = 0.10 Δt age gap in years (capped at 1) λ = 0.10

Candidates must share at least one rule; if none do (common for coding agents) the same kind family is used, then full-text matches. Terms neither decision has are dropped from the weighting. Scores ≥ 0.75 are strong precedent, ≥ 0.60 weak.

Tune in ~/.decisiontrace/config.toml:

[recall]
alpha = 0.3
lambda = 0.1
strong = 0.75
weak = 0.6
embeddings = "none"     # or "model2vec" with the [embeddings] extra

docs.title: dt ask
docs.text: Offline, questions are turned into filters — time window (today, yesterday, last week, last 30 days), outcome (reverted), exception, denied/rejected, approved, failed / over the limit, cost — plus full-text search. --llm lets Claude write the answer from the matching records (already redacted); nothing else is sent.

docs.title: Measuring it: dt eval
docs.text: dt eval --sample 20 -o golden.jsonl drafts cases from your real decisions; fill in what each explanation must mention, then dt eval golden.jsonl scores dt why (target 80%).

docs.title: DecisionTrace schema v0.1.0
docs.text: decisiontrace.schema.json is the canonical, open definition of a DecisionTrace record (JSON Schema 2020-12). Any tool can emit records that validate against it; this package is one implementation.

docs.title: Records
docs.text:
A store is an append-only sequence of three record types (record_type):

record_type Meaning decision One decision, DT = ⟨C, P, E, X, H, T, O⟩ outcome An outcome learned later, linked by trace_id (never an edit); an accepted one may carry a verified work unit (vwu) correction A correction to a decision, linked by trace_id; changes maps field paths to corrected values

docs.title: Decision fields
docs.text:
Paper Field Contents C context workflow, inputs[] (typed references, optional hash/summary), state_before P policies[] policy_id, version/hash, engine, result (pass/fail/not_applicable/error), enforced E exceptions[] Rule overridden, reason, granted_by, at X alternatives[] Action not taken + rejected_by (model/human/policy/system) and why H human_path[] Typed steps: requested, approved, rejected, edited, escalated, commented, overrode T actor_time actor, on_behalf_of, model, client, session_id, started_at/ended_at, cost O outcome Status known at record time; later outcomes are outcome records a_t actions[] What was actually done (tool call, API call, message, file/memory write, state change) S_t+1 state_after Reference to the resulting state (e.g. git commit)

Also: decision_kind (dotted label), intent (one redacted line), capabilities[] (inferred, never declared), links[] (typed edges: context, precedent, reversal, exec, delegation, hand_off, supersedes), attributes (namespaced extension keys), integrity (per-store hash chain, set by the store).

docs.title: Rules the schema encodes
docs.text:
• References, not copies. Context, state and diffs are pointers plus optional SHA-256. Bodies are not part of the record.
  • No reasoning. There is no field for model reasoning or chain-of-thought, and unknown fields are rejected.
  • Typed human path, so approvals per 100 decisions can be counted without parsing text.
  • Timestamps carry an offset; IDs are ULIDs (sortable by time).

docs.title: Verified work units
docs.text:
An accepted outcome record may carry vwu: one completed, accepted and reversible unit of work that met its quality threshold (the WorkRank paper's VWU).

Field Contents unit Dotted label for what one unit is, e.g. code.change, support.ticket quantity Units delivered (absent means 1) executor Who did the work (absent means the decision's actor) quality metric (definition id), threshold, value, baseline, direction (higher/lower) measured Measurement window: started_at, ended_at verification method (human, automated, outcome_signal, precedent, sample), at, verifier, ref reversal window_ends_at, max_cost_usd

Actors carry org (the accountable organisation, e.g. a vendor) and version (an agent's model, prompt and tool bundle). The schema rejects a unit on any status but accepted. JSON Schema cannot compare two values, so the reference implementation and dt validate also reject a value that misses its threshold and windows that end before they start.

docs.title: OpenTelemetry GenAI mapping
docs.text:
Pinned to opentelemetry-semantic-conventions 0.66b1. Fields carry an x-otel annotation.

DecisionTrace OTel attribute actor_time.model.provider gen_ai.provider.name actor_time.model.name gen_ai.request.model actor_time.session_id gen_ai.conversation.id actor_time.actor.id / .name (agents) gen_ai.agent.id / gen_ai.agent.name actor_time.cost.input_tokens gen_ai.usage.input_tokens actor_time.cost.output_tokens gen_ai.usage.output_tokens actor_time.cost.cache_read_input_tokens gen_ai.usage.cache_read.input_tokens actions[].name (tool calls) gen_ai.tool.name actions[].call_id gen_ai.tool.call.id context.workflow gen_ai.workflow.name

docs.title: Examples
docs.text: The schema/examples/ folder holds ten decisions (refunds, PR merge, Claude Code edit, email draft, denied tool call, escalated purchase order, memory write, delegation parent/child) plus two outcomes (one a reverted edit, one a verified work unit) and one correction. Validate any file with dt validate.

docs.title: User guide
docs.text:
DecisionTrace records why an AI-assisted decision was made, at the moment it happens: what was asked, which rules passed or failed, the exceptions and who granted them, the options that were rejected, who approved, and what happened afterwards. Everything stays on your machine in a local file. There is no account and no server.

This page walks through the whole lifecycle: install, record, recall, record outcomes, count verified work, keep the store trustworthy, and share one server with a team.

docs.title: 1. Install
docs.text:
You need Python 3.11 or newer.

sudo apt install pipx          # macOS: brew install pipx
pipx ensurepath                # then close and reopen the terminal
pipx install liquicent-decisiontrace
dt init                        # creates your store in ~/.decisiontrace
dt version                     # check it works

uv tool install liquicent-decisiontrace works instead of pipx. Inside a project's virtual environment, plain pip install liquicent-decisiontrace works too; outside one, Debian, Ubuntu and Homebrew Python refuse it with "externally-managed-environment". Upgrade later with pipx upgrade liquicent-decisiontrace.

docs.title: 2. Start recording
docs.text:
Pick the tool you already use:

You use Run this What happens Claude Code dt install claude-code Hooks record every decision in every project; --scope project records only this repo Claude Desktop dt install claude-desktop Adds the DecisionTrace MCP server: Claude can record, recall and log outcomes Cursor dt install cursor The same, for Cursor Your own Python agent client = dt.wrap(anthropic.Anthropic()) Each tool-use loop becomes one decision; openai.OpenAI() and the async clients work too An agent already traced with OpenTelemetry dt ingest-otel GenAI spans become decisions, with no code change A team on Claude.ai, ChatGPT or Claude Code A self-hosted server One connector URL for everyone; see section 7

Then work as usual. dt uninstall claude-code (or claude-desktop, cursor) stops recording; decisions already recorded are kept.

docs.title: In your own code
docs.text:
Your code enforces its rules; tell DecisionTrace what happened from inside the tool:

import anthropic, decisiontrace as dt

client = dt.wrap(anthropic.Anthropic())


def issue_refund(order_id, amount):
    if amount > 500:
        dt.policy("refund.max_auto_amount", "fail", detail=f"${amount} > $500", enforced=True)
        dt.exception("refund.max_auto_amount", "carrier damage", granted_by="Support lead")
        dt.approval("approved", by="Support lead")
    ...

Without an SDK:

with dt.decision("refund.approve", intent="Refund $850 for order 7731", agent="refunds") as d:
    d.context("order", "shop:7731", summary="arrived crushed")
    d.policy("refund.max_auto_amount", "fail", enforced=True)
    d.action("stripe.refunds.create", summary="Full refund $850", type="api_call")

Recording never raises into your code; problems go to ~/.decisiontrace/recorder-errors.log. More in Anthropic and OpenAI SDKs and OpenTelemetry.

docs.title: 3. Look back
docs.text:
dt log                               # recent decisions, newest first
dt show <id>                         # one decision in full
dt why <id>                          # a plain-English account (any unique start of the id)
dt why src/billing/due_dates.py      # the last decision that changed this file
dt why c1a90b2                       # the decision behind this git commit
dt similar <id>                      # past decisions like it, with the similarity breakdown
dt ask "what did we revert last week?"   # offline; --llm uses Claude

See Recall for how similarity and dt ask work.

docs.title: 4. Record what happened
docs.text:
A decision teaches something only once its outcome is known. Outcomes are appended as new records; the decision itself is never edited.

By hand:

dt outcome <id> --accepted
dt outcome <id> --reverted --note "broke month-end invoices"
dt outcome <id> --complained --value-usd -250

Other outcomes: --overridden, --escalated, --failed.

Automatically, from signals that already exist (safe to run every day, for example from cron):

dt outcomes detect                                   # overrides and reversals in the store
dt outcomes detect --git ~/src/app                   # git reverts and merges
dt outcomes detect --events tickets.jsonl --preset zendesk
dt outcomes detect --assume-accepted-after 14        # opt-in: no complaint in 14 days = accepted
dt outcomes detect --dry-run                         # preview; writes nothing

Presets: stripe, zendesk, jira, github, pagerduty, or generic JSON Lines. An outcome a person recorded is never overridden. Details in Outcome detection.

docs.title: 5. Count verified work
docs.text:
A verified work unit (VWU) is one piece of accepted work that met its quality bar and can still be undone at a known cost.

dt outcome <id> --accepted --vwu code.change --verified-by automated \
  --reversal-days 3 --reversal-cost 150 \
  --quality-metric ci.required_checks/v1 --quality-threshold 1 --quality-value 1

dt outcomes detect --git . --vwu      # merged, unreverted commits become code.change units
dt vwu                                # every unit, its state, and who did the work

A unit is provisional inside its reversal window, final after it, and reverted if it was undone in time. The footer of dt vwu shows the share of units checked without a person. See Verified work units.

docs.title: 6. Keep it trustworthy
docs.text:
dt verify                          # recompute the hash chain; reports any tampering
dt export -o export.jsonl          # every record, for backup or for Valence
dt validate records.jsonl          # check records against the schema without storing them
  • Secrets (API keys, tokens, passwords) are removed before anything is written.
  • Emails, phone numbers, cards, PAN and Aadhaar become stable pseudonyms.
  • Model reasoning and assistant replies are never stored; prompt and response bodies only if you set bodies = true in ~/.decisiontrace/config.toml.
  • dt verify prints the head hash: save it somewhere you trust to anchor the chain.

See Privacy & security.

docs.title: 7. Teams: one shared server
docs.text:
Run one DecisionTrace server; Claude.ai, ChatGPT, Claude Code and your agents connect to it.

export DT_MCP_TOKEN=$(dt mcp --new-token)        # keep it in your secret store
DT_HOME=/srv/decisiontrace dt mcp --http --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8765 --allowed-host dt.yourco.com

Or use the Docker setup in deploy/self-hosted-mcp/: copy .env.example to .env, set your host and token, then docker compose up -d --build (Caddy obtains the HTTPS certificate).

Tool Setup Claude.ai (an owner adds it for the organisation) Custom connector: https://dt.yourco.com/t/<token>/mcp ChatGPT business workspace An admin adds a custom MCP connector at the same URL Claude Code claude mcp add --transport http decisiontrace https://dt.yourco.com/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer $DT_MCP_TOKEN"

The server must be reachable over HTTPS from the internet: connectors call it from the AI provider's cloud. Full guide: Self-hosted MCP.

docs.title: 8. Try it without any setup
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/Liquicent/liquicent-decisiontrace && cd liquicent-decisiontrace
uv sync
uv run python examples/refund_agent.py   # offline demo; --live uses real Claude
uv run dt log
uv run dt why <id from the log>

docs.title: Quick reference
docs.text:
Task Command Start recording dt install claude-code What happened today dt log Why did it do that? dt why <id / file / commit> Has this come up before? dt similar <id> How did it turn out? dt outcome <id> --accepted or dt outcomes detect --git . Verified work dt vwu Is the record intact? dt verify Stop recording dt uninstall claude-code Help on any command dt <command> --help

Every command is listed in the CLI reference.

docs.title: Verified work units
docs.text:
A verified work unit (VWU) is one completed, accepted and reversible unit of work that met its quality and governance thresholds. The definition comes from the WorkRank paper. It counts outcomes, not effort, time or process.

A unit is recorded on an accepted outcome record, so the decision itself is never edited:

dt outcome 01M4ZDRZG0 --accepted --vwu code.change \
  --verified-by automated --reversal-days 3 --reversal-cost 150 \
  --quality-metric ci.required_checks/v1 --quality-threshold 1 --quality-value 1
dt outcomes detect --git . --vwu      # merged, unreverted commits become code.change units
dt vwu                                # every unit, its state, and who did the work

docs.title: What a unit records
docs.text:
Field Holds unit What one unit is, a dotted label: code.change, support.ticket, sales.close quantity Units delivered (absent means 1) executor Who did the work (absent means the decision's actor) quality The predefined threshold: metric id, threshold, value, baseline, direction measured The measurement window: started_at, ended_at verification method (human, automated, outcome_signal, precedent, sample), at, verifier, ref reversal window_ends_at (until when it can be undone) and max_cost_usd (what undoing costs)

A value that misses its threshold is not a unit and is rejected. The same goes for a window that ends before the verification, and for a unit on any status but accepted.

docs.title: Who earns from a unit
docs.text: Whoever executed it: a person, an agent, or a vendor's person or agent. The Actor record carries org, the accountable organisation the executor works for, and version, an agent's model, prompt and tool bundle. Trust earned by one agent version need not carry to the next. DecisionTrace records who did the work; it never scores them. Trust, routing and settlement need many people's records and live in Liquicent.

docs.title: State
docs.text:
A unit's state is derived when you read it, never stored:

  • provisional: still inside its reversal window.
  • final: the window has ended with no cancel. A cancel after the window does not reopen it.
  • reverted: a later outcome for the same decision was reverted, failed or overridden inside the window. A complaint or an escalation does not undo delivery.

docs.title: The number to watch
docs.text: dt vwu ends with the share of units verified without a person. When agents produce far more units than people can review, that share decides how fast work can be accepted. Checks that run by themselves (automated, outcome_signal, precedent, sample) are what keep review from becoming the bottleneck.

docs.title: Claude Code adapter
docs.text: Records one DecisionTrace per prompt you give Claude Code: what you asked, what it read, what it changed, which permission checks ran, what was proposed but not done, what you approved or denied, the model, tokens, and the git commit before and after.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
pipx install liquicent-decisiontrace   # see Getting started if pip refuses
dt install claude-code            # all projects (~/.claude/settings.json)
dt install claude-code --scope project   # this repo, committed (.claude/settings.json)
dt install claude-code --scope local     # this repo, just you (.claude/settings.local.json)

Work as usual, then:

dt log
dt show <id>

Remove with dt uninstall claude-code (your recorded decisions are kept). Existing hooks and settings are preserved; a backup is written next to the settings file.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
1. A hook (python -I -S …/hook.py) runs on UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure, PermissionRequest, PermissionDenied, SubagentStart, SubagentStop, Stop, StopFailure and SessionEnd.
  2. It redacts the event and appends one line to ~/.decisiontrace/queue/<session>.jsonl. It uses only the standard library: median ~35 ms, always exits 0, prints nothing, never makes a decision.
  3. When a turn ends, a background drain groups the events by prompt_id, builds the decision, reads model/tokens/version from the transcript, and appends it to the store. dt log and dt show also drain first.

docs.title: What maps where
docs.text:
Claude Code DecisionTrace your prompt intent (redacted summary) + context.inputs[user_prompt] (hash) Read / Grep / Glob, WebFetch context.inputs (files, URLs) git HEAD at prompt / at stop context.state_before / state_after tool calls that ran actions (file_write, memory_write for CLAUDE.md and .claude/, tool_call) permission outcome per tool policies (permission:<Tool>, engine claude_code_permissions) denied, auto-denied, interrupted, blocked calls alternatives with rejected_by human / policy / system permission prompt + your answer human_path (requested, approved / rejected, latency) subagent work its own decision, linked from the parent by a delegation link model, tokens, Claude Code version actor_time.model, .cost, .client

decision_kind and capabilities are inferred from the tools used (e.g. code.edit, code.commit, harness.update) — you never declare them.

docs.title: Never recorded
docs.text: Claude's reasoning, its replies, file contents, command output. Prompt bodies are stored only if you set bodies = true in ~/.decisiontrace/config.toml; otherwise a hash and a redacted summary.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• Nothing in dt log: run dt drain; check ~/.decisiontrace/hook-errors.log.
  • Using a custom store location: Claude Code must see the same DT_HOME.
  • Events that fail to build are kept in ~/.decisiontrace/queue/failed/, never dropped.

docs.title: MCP server
docs.text:
dt mcp runs a local MCP server (stdio) named decisiontrace with three tools:

Tool Use it to record Write a decision from a client without hooks: intent, rules checked (pass/fail), exceptions and who granted them, rejected options, approvals, actions, outcome recall Ask "have we decided something like this before?" — returns precedents with their rules, exceptions, approval path and outcome, not just text. Pass a decision id to rank by the DecisionTrace similarity function instead outcome Attach what happened to a past decision

The server ships instructions telling the model to recall before rule/limit/exception decisions and to record facts only — never secrets or its own reasoning. Everything is redacted before it reaches the local store.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
dt install claude-desktop      # writes claude_desktop_config.json (backup kept)
dt install cursor              # writes ~/.cursor/mcp.json
dt mcp --config claude-code    # prints: claude mcp add --scope user decisiontrace -- …

Restart the app. Then ask, for example: "How did we handle the last refund over the limit?" — the model calls recall and answers with the past decision, who waived the limit and why.

To print the JSON for any other MCP client: dt mcp --config cursor. Remove with dt uninstall claude-desktop / dt uninstall cursor.

docs.title: Example recall result
docs.text:
{
  "precedents": [
    {
      "id": "01M53…",
      "kind": "refund.approve",
      "intent": "Refund $850 for order 7731, parcel crushed in transit",
      "rules": [{"rule": "refund.max_auto_amount", "result": "fail",
                 "detail": "Amount $850 exceeds the $500 limit"}],
      "exceptions": [{"rule": "refund.max_auto_amount", "waived_by": "Meera",
                      "role": "support lead", "reason": "VIP and carrier damage confirmed"}],
      "approval_path": [{"step": "requested", "by": "refunds agent"},
                        {"step": "approved", "by": "Meera"}],
      "outcome": "accepted",
      "score": 0.97
    }
  ]
}

For a team, or for Claude.ai and ChatGPT workspace connectors, run the same tools on your own server: self-hosted MCP.

docs.title: OpenTelemetry
docs.text:
Already instrumented with OpenTelemetry GenAI spans? Don't change the agent — point its exporter at DecisionTrace:

dt ingest-otel                          # listens on http://127.0.0.1:4318/v1/traces
export OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://localhost:4318

OTLP/HTTP JSON works out of the box; protobuf (the default for most exporters) needs pip install 'liquicent-decisiontrace[otel]'. Files from a collector's file exporter: dt ingest-otel --file spans.json. Re-ingesting the same spans never duplicates.

Span DecisionTrace gen_ai.operation.name = invoke_agent (else the trace root) one decision; nested agents become linked decisions execute_tool spans actions (gen_ai.tool.name, gen_ai.tool.call.id, error status → failed) gen_ai.request/response.model, gen_ai.provider.name, gen_ai.usage.* actor_time.model, .cost gen_ai.conversation.id, gen_ai.agent.id/name actor_time.session_id, .actor attributes decisiontrace.intent, decisiontrace.decision_kind intent, decision_kind span events decisiontrace.policy (policy_id, result, detail, enforced) policies span events decisiontrace.exception (policy_id, reason, granted_by) exceptions span events decisiontrace.approval (step, by, detail) human_path span events decisiontrace.rejected (name, by, reason) alternatives

Never read: gen_ai.input.messages, gen_ai.output.messages, gen_ai.system_instructions, tool results. Tool arguments are hashed. Conventions pinned to opentelemetry-semantic-conventions 0.66b1.

Example: uv run python examples/otel_agent.py.

docs.title: Anthropic and OpenAI SDKs
docs.text:
import anthropic, decisiontrace as dt

client = dt.wrap(anthropic.Anthropic())  # or openai.OpenAI(), AsyncAnthropic(), AsyncOpenAI()

That's the only change. Each tool-use loop — from the first user message until the model stops asking for tools — becomes one DecisionTrace:

Seen in the loop Recorded as first user message intent + context.inputs[user_prompt] (hash + redacted summary) tool calls whose results came back actions (failed if the result was an error) tool calls proposed but never answered alternatives, rejected by system model, token usage across the loop actor_time.model, .cost

Covered: messages.create, messages.parse, messages.stream and their beta versions (so the SDK's tool runner is recorded too); OpenAI Chat Completions and Responses. Raw stream=True iterators are passed through but not recorded.

docs.title: Recording rules, exceptions and approvals
docs.text:
Your code enforces the rules; tell DecisionTrace what happened from inside the tool:

def issue_refund(order_id, amount):
    if amount > 500:
        dt.policy("refund.max_auto_amount", "fail", detail=f"${amount} > $500", enforced=True)
        if not approved_by_lead():
            dt.approval("rejected", by="Meera (support lead)")
            return {"status": "denied"}
        dt.exception("refund.max_auto_amount", "carrier damage", granted_by="Meera (support lead)")
        dt.approval("approved", by="Meera (support lead)")
    ...

These calls attach to the loop being recorded and do nothing outside one.

docs.title: Without an SDK
docs.text:
with dt.decision("refund.approve", intent="Refund $850 for order 7731", agent="refunds") as d:
    d.context("order", "shop:7731", summary="arrived crushed")
    d.policy("refund.max_auto_amount", "fail", enforced=True)
    d.exception("refund.max_auto_amount", "VIP", granted_by="Meera (support lead)")
    d.action("stripe.refunds.create", summary="Full refund $850", type="api_call")

Recording never raises into your code; errors go to ~/.decisiontrace/recorder-errors.log.

Example: uv run python examples/refund_agent.py (offline; --live for real Claude).

docs.title: Self-hosted MCP server (for teams)
docs.text:
dt mcp --http serves DecisionTrace's three tools (record, recall, outcome) over HTTPS from the company's own infrastructure, so a whole team can use them: Claude.ai and ChatGPT workspace connectors, Claude Code, and the company's own agents. Records go into one store the company controls; nothing is sent anywhere else.

Claude.ai / ChatGPT connector ─┐
Claude Code (remote MCP) ──────┼──HTTPS──> reverse proxy (TLS) ──> dt mcp --http ──> /data (traces.db)
Company agents (MCP client) ───┘

What it records. A decision is recorded when the assistant calls record (the server's instructions ask it to, around rules, limits, exceptions and approvals). It is not a transcript of every conversation. For complete capture of developer work use the Claude Code hooks (dt install claude-code); for your own agents use the SDK wrapper.

docs.title: 1. Run it
docs.text:
export DT_MCP_TOKEN=$(dt mcp --new-token)        # keep it in your secret store
DT_HOME=/srv/decisiontrace dt mcp --http --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8765 --allowed-host dt.acme.com
Option Default Meaning --http off Serve over HTTP instead of stdio --host, --port 127.0.0.1, 8765 Where to listen --token / DT_MCP_TOKEN none Shared token, at least 24 characters. Required on any host other than localhost --tools record,recall,outcome Tools to expose. Use record,outcome if precedents should not be readable by everyone with access --client-name mcp-http Stored as the client on every decision (e.g. claude.ai connector) --allowed-host none Accepted Host header(s), e.g. your public name (repeatable) --access-log off Log requests. Leave off: logs would contain the secret URL

Endpoints: POST /mcp (header token), POST /t/<token>/mcp (secret URL), GET /healthz (ok, no token, no data). Responses are plain JSON (stateless streamable HTTP), so several replicas can share one volume behind a load balancer if needed; one is plenty for most teams.

docs.title: With Docker and automatic HTTPS
docs.text:
deploy/self-hosted-mcp/ holds a Dockerfile, compose.yaml and a Caddyfile:

cd deploy/self-hosted-mcp
cp .env.example .env            # set DT_PUBLIC_HOST=dt.acme.com and DT_MCP_TOKEN
docker compose up -d --build    # Caddy obtains the TLS certificate for DT_PUBLIC_HOST
curl https://dt.acme.com/healthz

The store lives in the dt-data volume. Back it up like any database volume.

docs.title: 2. Connect clients
docs.text:
Connector screens change names often; look for "custom connector" or "MCP server" in your admin console.

Client How URL / setting Claude.ai (Team / Enterprise: an owner adds it for the organisation; individual plans: in your own settings) Add a custom connector https://dt.acme.com/t/<token>/mcp ChatGPT (business workspaces that allow custom MCP connectors) An admin adds a custom connector / MCP server, no authentication https://dt.acme.com/t/<token>/mcp Claude Code claude mcp add --transport http decisiontrace https://dt.acme.com/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer $DT_MCP_TOKEN" header token Your agents Any MCP client over streamable HTTP https://dt.acme.com/mcp + Authorization: Bearer <token>

Connectors are called from the AI provider's cloud, not from the employee's browser, so the server must be reachable from the internet over HTTPS. Where the provider publishes its egress IP ranges, restrict the reverse proxy to them.

docs.title: 3. Security model
docs.text:
• One shared token. Anyone with it can call the exposed tools. Treat the secret URL like a password: share it only through the admin console, rotate it by restarting with a new token (then update the connector), and use --tools record,outcome for broad rollouts.
  • No user identity. Connectors do not tell the server who the employee is. The assistant may pass on_behalf_of (e.g. "Meera (support lead)"); otherwise the decision has no principal. The server never attributes decisions to its own OS account.
  • Same privacy as local use. Secrets and personal data are redacted before write, no prompt bodies are stored, model reasoning is never stored, and the store is hash-chained (dt verify).
  • Refusals. The server will not start off localhost without a token, or with a token shorter than 24 characters. Without a token on localhost it checks the Host header (DNS-rebinding protection).
  • The conversation itself is processed by the AI provider as usual; DecisionTrace only receives what the assistant sends to its tools.

docs.title: 4. Operate
docs.text:
docker compose exec decisiontrace dt verify
docker compose exec decisiontrace dt log -n 20
docker compose exec decisiontrace dt outcomes detect --assume-accepted-after 14   # e.g. daily from cron
docker compose exec decisiontrace dt export -o /data/export.jsonl                 # for Valence / Liquicent
